title: review: goal start: a second goal in the same repo must not switch the shared checkout and drop the first goal's tasks from the bus
spec:
Evidence (luna-inbox 2026-10-07 21:10): `orchestrator goal start luna-inbox ...` for T-0615 while goal T-0609 was live
committed T-0609's bookkeeping to goal/T-0609 (26fe512), then checked out goal/T-0615 cut from main in the repo root.
The bus is the JSON files under .orchestrator/tasks in that checkout, so T-0594..T-0614 vanished from the bus: the daemon
and bus.get no longer saw T-0609's queued tasks (T-0610..T-0613) or T-0614's gate result, and plan.md became T-0615's.
The Planner restored the missing task files from goal/T-0609 by hand at 21:40.
Fix (orchestrator/goals.py or wherever goal start lives, plus cli.py if needed):
1. goal start never switches the repo root's branch when another goal in that repo is live (not done/superseded); it
   keeps the current checkout and records the new goal's branch name only (task merges already target goal/<parent>
   through merge.py, independent of the checked-out branch).
2. Each goal keeps its own plan file (.orchestrator/plan-<goal>.md, with plan.md pointing at the live goals) so two
   headless Planners do not overwrite one plan.md; the decision-packet path reads the goal's own plan file.
3. If the root must be on a goal branch for a single live goal (existing behaviour), keep that path unchanged.
Tests (tests/test_goals.py or the existing goal-start test module): test_second_goal_start_keeps_checkout_and_bus,
test_each_goal_reads_its_own_plan_file.
Run the relevant unittest modules. Commit on the task branch.
acceptance: a second goal start in a repo with a live goal leaves the checkout branch and every task file in place
each goal Planner reads and writes its own plan file

result.summary: The diff meets all three acceptance criteria. A second goal start keeps the checkout and every task file, and only records and creates the new goal/<id> branch. Each goal gets its own plan-<id>.md. The two named tests exist as unittest methods and assert the right things. I did not run them. The comments below are minor.

comments.issue: The single-live-goal path is not fully unchanged. Every goal now gets a plan-<id>.md and a prompt line telling the Planner to use it instead of plan.md, even when no other goal is live. Hooks, handover and the CLAUDE.md protocol still reference plan.md, so a lone goal's Planner may split its state between the two files. Acceptance criterion 3 asks for the existing path to stay as it is.

_live_goal_ids counts any goal whose status is not done or superseded, so failed or cancelled goals count as live. A second start after a failed goal then takes the no-checkout path and rewrites plan.md with a live-goals block.

The pointer block is written into the shared plan.md without a lock. Two concurrent goal starts can race on the read-modify-write and drop a pointer line. Starts are probably serialized by the running-slot reservation, so the risk is small.
